title: Guarding the U.S. against Adversarial Robotics Dominance Act of 2026 (GUARD Act of 2026)
sponsor: Rep. John R. Moolenaar (introduced for himself, Rep. Jay Obernolte, and Rep. Jennifer McClellan)
committee: House Committee on Energy and Commerce
status: H.R. 9129: 2026-09-01 — Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: Directs an appropriate national-security agency to determine within one year whether covered humanoid/quadruped robotics communications equipment or services pose an unacceptable risk to U.S. national security or the safety/security of U.S. persons. If the agency does not make a determination by the deadline, the FCC must add all covered equipment/services to its covered list; affirmative findings trigger listing and reporting. A negative finding requires reporting and review by other appropriate national-security agencies.
mechanism_scope_limitations: Covers humanoid or quadruped ground robots, their control software/external devices, when they are communications equipment or services produced/provided by a covered foreign entity (including entities tied to a country of concern through control, ownership, joint venture, or technology-sharing/licensing). The bill provides a path to avoid listing on a timely negative determination; it does not itself impose a direct across-the-board procurement or private ownership ban.

quotes.quote: If the appropriate national security agency does not make a determination as required by paragraph (1) within 1 year after the enactment of this Act, the Commission shall add all covered robotics communications equipment or services to the covered list.
H.R. 9129, H.R. 6152, H.R. 2805, and H.R. 4950 were forwarded to the full Committee, without amendment.
